title: Akulakhan s Chamber needs 18.8 MB for its models and textures with its activators kept: more than the 14.3 MB the 32 MB minimum gives a room, so the image step stops
status: Fixed in source on v0.0.52 (commit d0d2f04b, gate 3944, 25 October 2026), the dev1 build to confirm: a room map holds nothing but its room (the maintainer: just that place and Dagoth Ur), so a CHIM room whose models do not fit its zone and the cache bank now grows under the loading plaque (engine/aga/src/chim/chim_world.c Chim_RoomGrow, chim_room.c ChimRoom_Begin): first a bank of the free Fast RAM (its largest block less 2 MiB, whole MiB), then the game heap s rest past its zone (chim_reserve_kib and what the map loads after the zone kept), both given back at the next map; rooms that fit take neither. Measured in FS-UAE at 32 MB in a room map (the v0.0.51 final image, Akulakhan s Chamber with Dagoth Ur): 6,222 KiB of free Fast RAM in one block, so a 4 MiB room bank; the heap s rest adds 2,094,736 bytes. The image s room heap gate (tools/chim/heap.py) now counts the same steps and the engine s own blocks (the record with its 379 placements, every model and texture, the store index, the prefetch table) and loads a room past one bank through the engine s own allocator (tools/chim/room_zone.py): Akulakhan s Chamber needs 19,093,616 bytes, 32 MB gives a room 20,625,040 (was 14,336,000), 1.53 MB to spare, every model kept (the Heart and Akulakhan); Dagoth Ur s actor model 768 KB at most in Quake s cache, within the 2 MiB gap. All 1,132 rooms of the stopped image pass; 25 are marked for 32 MB (18 before: the store index and the placements were not counted). The early check: the chim-interiors stage checks the store as soon as it is written (chim-room-heap-early.json, 18 s on 8 workers), so a room that cannot fit stops a build there, not 39 minutes into it in the image step. Watch (2026-10-25 22:59 +0200 / 2026-10-25 20:59 UTC): the first measuring run (gate 3940 s v0.0.52 engine on the v0.0.51 final image, mixed versions: aw_clip is not a field warnings) froze about 150 s into Akulakhan s Chamber just after a chim console command; the second run (chim at 40 s) passed. Probably the version mix; checked in the dev1 boot check (Akulakhan s Chamber, the chim command, two minutes). Confirmed by the build (2026-10-25 23:54 +0200 / 2026-10-25 21:54 UTC, v0.0.52-dev1-try3): the image room gate passed it, 19,093,616 of 20,625,024 bytes at 32 MB, marked for 32 MB. In-game check still to do. Risk (2026-10-26 02:47 +0200 / 2026-10-26 00:47 UTC): the skeletal actors' shared tables take free Fast RAM outside the heap and shrink the room bank this fix relies on (see SKEL-HEAP-ACCOUNTING-52); to be measured in the skeletal dev1 image before the release. Correction (28 October 2026): the 'aw_clip' is not a field lines were blamed on mixed versions; wrong: every CHIM room load prints them once per clip wall (AW-CLIP-NOT-A-FIELD-54).
severity_reason: The dev1 build cannot finish; the final room of the main quest

reports.note: In game, 32 MB from Balmora: 379 placements, 148 models 18129 KiB loaded whole; zone 804 KiB free; nothing failed; Dagoth Ur in front of Akulakhan

title: The m68k compiler crashed on the animation table parse (internal compiler error in patch_jump_insn); the host tests compile it with the host compiler only
status: Fixed (2026-10-25 22:45 +0200 / 2026-10-25 20:45 UTC, a34723eb): AW_SkelParse with its three validation loops and early returns in one function made gcc 16.2.0b for m68k fail at -O1 (aw_skel.c:75, patch_jump_insn); each check is now its own function and aw_skel.c, aw_skel_load.c and r_alias.c compile with the gate flags. Early check to add: the skeleton native test also compiles aw_skel.c with the m68k compiler when the image has it (seconds, instead of the full gate engine step). Seen again (2026-10-25 22:52 +0200 / 2026-10-25 20:52 UTC, gate 3943 on a34723eb): the split alone was not enough: the 68060 hard-float -O1 build (one of the engine variants; my first check compiled only 68040 -O1) still crashed at the parse's closing brace. Reproduced with that variant; the checks are now never inlined (AW_SKEL_APART), and aw_skel.c, aw_skel_load.c and r_alias.c compile in 68040 -O1/-O2 and 68060 hard-float -O1/-O2. The quick check (every variant, each compiler exit code, seconds) is the early check to fold into the native test.
severity_reason: The engine would not build; found only by the full gate engine step

title: Skeletal actors draw no carried weapon, shield or torch: the item tags hold one row per model frame, and a skeletal model has every table frame
status: In progress (2026-10-26 00:02 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:02 UTC): a per-frame row for all 2,730 table frames would be about 230 KB of text per armed actor. New tag form AWTS1 (the builder: the item paths, the weapon and shield bone indices in the table, the actor scale): the engine (aw_items.c AW_ItemsParseSkel, 93f0272c) poses the table at the actor s frame and makes the row from the bone (aw_skel.c AW_SkelBoneTag, equal to npc_items.quake_angles within 0.002 degrees; its angles from a polynomial atan, since the library s atan2/asin compile to FATAN/FASIN, which the 68040 lacks and the engine audit refused in gate 3946). Open: the builder writing AWTS1 for skeletal residents; the guard torches on the same path; the in-game check. Builder side (2026-10-26 00:13 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:13 UTC): every armed skeletal resident gets its AWTS1 tag (tools/skeletal_actor.py skeletal_tag: the item model paths, the table's weapon bone and shield bone indices, the actor scale; read_skeletal_tag reads it back, tests/test_npc_anim_type.py); the item models are written as before. Still a release blocker for type 2 until the guard torches are on the same path and both are seen in the game. Guard torches (2026-10-26 00:43 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:43 UTC): today prepare_guard_torches.py bakes a body and a held torch model per guard type (8 or 21 frames) and a per-frame flame table (gfx/guard-torches.awg), another per-actor bake that does not fit skeletal guards. Design for type 2: the torch is the guard s shield-slot item in its AWTS1 tag (the item model carries the carried-light rotation and BoneOffset, so its frame is the shield bone s), with an optional line emitter x y z: the torch s fire emitter point in the shield bone s space; the engine places the flame and its light from the item pose each frame (aw_guard_torch.c for skeletal guards). The AWG1 registry stays for type 1 only. Guard torches, builder side (2026-10-26 00:54 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:54 UTC): a torch-carrying guard (prepare_guard_torches.guard_eligibility) baked skeletal names the torch item on a 'light PATH' line beside its own shield (prepare_guard_torches.torch_item: the original 238 triangles in the shield bone's axes, carried-light rotation and BoneOffset applied; the engine shows it by the day and night cycle) and an 'emitter X Y Z' line after it (the fire emitter point in the shield bone's space, unscaled) in its AWTS1 tag; the image step's guard torch registry (AWG1) leaves skeletal guards out (skeletal_actor.is_skeletal). Checked on the base game's data: 12 torch-carrying guard records; company guard_unique and hlaalu guard bake with weapon, torch and emitter. Open: the engine drawing the flame and light from the item pose (aw_guard_torch.c), the in-game check. Seen in v0.0.52-dev2 (2026-10-26 11:18 +0200 / 2026-10-26 09:18 UTC, FS-UAE JIT, 32 MB, image 3715e8c4): at 22:00 in Balmora (bm1, dbg set time 2200, the automatic cycle: Guard torches auto, automatic night) a skeletal Hlaalu guard staged before the camera (dbg animkit stage 3: common table, weapon, shield, carried light) holds no torch and casts no light. A few flame-like pixels lie on the ground to his left, about his height away. The torch entity or its flame point is placed away from his shield bone. The baked guard registry reported 4 eligible and 4 admitted. Stills and a 15 s clip: clips/v0.0.52 balmora_night_skeletal_guard (with a headlamp-on zoom). Not looked into yet: the guard in his own place (not moved by the stage), and whether the torch model is drawn at all. 2026-10-26 12:53 +0200 / 2026-10-26 10:53 UTC: the night torch, checked with a guard in his own place (Seyda Neen sn1, 22:00, automatic cycle; guard lights active 2): real. The torch was drawn as a horizontal stick from the left hand with its flame particles falling beside him. Two causes, both fixed in the engine (gate 4034): (1) the skeletal guard kept his arm down: the baked guards hold the torch with the left arm (Bip01 L Clavicle down) on the table's torch group (prepare_guard_torches.TorchLayer), the skeletal pose did not; the table's shield bone matched the NIF exactly (checked on the maintainer's data), so the item was right and the arm wrong. Now AW_SkelPoseLayer poses the left arm from the torch group (frames 667-688 of humanoid.awsk, in turn with the actor's frame) while torches are shown, for the drawn model, its cull box and the item rows (aw_items.c AW_ItemsTorchLayer; the arm root found as the shield bone's fourth ancestor beside the weapon bone's, no builder change). (2) The flame point was used in the shield bone's units in the item's 0.25-scale space, about three torch lengths out: now taken at the item scale. After (same place and time, new engine): the arm raised, the torch at the shoulder, the flame and smoke from its head. Stills and a clip: clips/v0.0.52 skel_guard_torch (before, after, crops side by side). Test: tests/test_skel_native.py SkelTorchLayerNativeTests (layer pose against the builder's, the root rule and its refusals). 2026-10-26 13:02 +0200 / 2026-10-26 11:02 UTC: committed 9741c99c (gate 4034 passed, 5,913 tests); in-game check in the dev3 image.
severity_reason: Release blocker for skeletal actors: armed residents and the guard torches would be lost

reports.note: Confirmed in the dev3 image: Seyda Neen guard at 22:00 raises the torch at his shoulder, flame and smoke; Guard lights: active 2

title: The builder s readers of actor models refused or misjudged a skeletal model: the ground check stopped the build, the stream estimate called it unstreamable
status: Fixed in the working tree (2026-10-26 02:44 +0200 / 2026-10-26 00:44 UTC): both readers decoded a model and required it to end after its last frame; a skeletal model has one rest frame and then its AWSB block (76 + 16 bytes a vertex). The ground check now grounds the rest frame (the idle pose) and accepts a block of exactly that size; the stream estimate counts the model as streamed, as the engine s stream reader reads the block. Tests on a real skeletal model (tests/test_skeletal_actor.py). The gate had no test running these readers on a skeletal model; the rest of the builder s model readers (the decoded-size and heap estimates of actors) to be audited for the block: SKEL-HEAP-ACCOUNTING-52. PERSISTING after 9f481072 (2026-10-26 03:11 +0200 / 2026-10-26 01:11 UTC, the animation stage build, --miniwind-anim-stage --npc-anim-type 2, SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52): chim-town-balmora stopped again: Animation kit idle group outside the model frames. A skeletal actor's layout (idle:0:21, walk:1102:8 ...) names frames of its shared table (2,730); the ground check ran it against the model's one stored frame. The payload preflight's actor-frames check (tools/actor_frames.py audit_payload) had the same mistake three times: the layout against the header's 1 frame and the 256-frame ceiling, the aw_npc idle rule (exactly 0..7), the tag magic AWTG1 (a skeletal tag is AWTS1 FRAMES). Fixed in the working tree: model_frames gives a skeletal model's rest frame as RestFrame, grounded as its idle pose whatever the layout (check_actor_ground idle_poses); actor_frames.skeletal_frames reads the table frame count from the block (u32 at +48), of_model(skeletal=True) checks a layout against the table (up to 65,535 frames), a skeletal aw_npc's idle starts at table frame 0 with at least 8 frames (the QuakeC idle steps 0..7 inside it), tag_frames reads AWTS1. Tests: tests/test_skeletal_actor.py SkeletalModelReadersTests (gate 3962). Lesson (2026-10-26 03:40 +0200 / 2026-10-26 01:40 UTC): three dev1 stops in a row on the skeletal path (the ground check, the actor-frame checks, the image payload preflight not knowing .awsk), each late in a 1-hour build: the type-2 path had no end-to-end build before dev1. Early check: the animation-stage MiniWind build (SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52) on the same commit runs ahead of each dev build and found the last two first; a small skeletal MiniWind build belongs in the release flow before every dev build of a change to the actor path. PERSISTING, third stop (2026-10-26 03:47 +0200 / 2026-10-26 01:47 UTC, stage build try3 on 48b6738d): with the ground and actor-frames checks through, the image step's payload preflight refused the shared tables: file-formats: progs/humanoid.awsk, humanoid_f.awsk and humanoid_kna.awsk have a format the image step does not know. Fixed in 75200298: .awsk is an opaque payload format in tools/sky_palette_overlay.py (bone rotations and positions, no pixels); tools/map_engine_limits.py also counts the item precaches of an AWTS1 tag (weapon, shield, carried light), where before it counted AWTG1 tags only. Tests: test_payload_preflight FileFormatTests, test_map_engine_limits test_skeletal_actor_tags_count_their_items_and_light. Fourth stop (2026-10-26 04:33 +0200 / 2026-10-26 02:33 UTC, dev1-try8 9d4c05f7): the image step's actor placement gate (finalize, 25 minutes in): 2 skeletal residents fail ground contact (Hefadmir, Wusha; given to a worker). Early check to add: the actor contact check per model right after the resident and actor-library stages (their models are final there), so a grounding fault stops the build in that stage, not in the image. Process (rule 8, failures in a row): the skeletal MiniWind stage build now runs ahead of each dev build on the same commit.
severity_reason: The first build with skeletal actors stopped in chim-town-seyda

title: Two skeletal residents found no standing spot in their CHIM rooms: the rest frame soles came out unlike the baked idle soles
status: Found 2026-10-26 04:33 +0200 / 2026-10-26 02:33 UTC in dev1-try8 (2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev1_dev1-try8_9d4c05f7): the image step actor placement gate stopped on 2 unresolved cases, Hefadmir (Nord, base_anim, reference 299235, room ri16a0c0eea6, soles 2.67 to 3.86 units above support or unsupported) and Wusha (Argonian, base_animkna, reference 280101, room ridbab470875); the CHIM room actor bake had tried all 28,917 spots and refused both, where dev1-try4 (the baked kit) fitted them 12 and 14 units from their authored spots on sloped floors. Not a beast-table fault (Hefadmir is a Nord). Cause, measured with the room fitter on the try8 rooms: (1) the skeletal model was reduced from the 8 idle samples alone, the baked kit from every pose of its profile, so the reduced soles differ (Wusha: other sole points in the half-unit band); (2) its quantisation box spans every table frame, so its z grid fell where it fell and the soles came out up to a step above their true height, the check then taking in points 0.5 above them (Hefadmir: soles spread 0.5 units in height against the baked idle 0.15). Fixed in source: skeletal_resident reduces from the baked kit own samples (npc_anim.plan, the first sample the rest pose), and the z grid puts the rest pose lowest point on a step (skeletal_actor.ground_grid). Rebaked on the maintainer data, both fit their try8 rooms (Hefadmir at attempt 1,514, Wusha at 2,623) and the packaged check passes at the fitted spots (sole gaps -0.48 to 0.99). Tests: test_skeletal_actor (the rest frame on its true soles), test_npc_anim_type (reduced from the kit poses). Open: seen in the next dev1 build.
severity_reason: The image step actor placement gate stops the build (dev1-try8)

title: A reused stage recreates, as empty folders, the folders another stage filled beside it: the area stage then stops on its own room folder
status: Found 2026-10-26 05:18 +0200 / 2026-10-26 03:18 UTC in dev1-try9 (2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev1_dev1-try9_9a95fb79, reusing try8): the area stage stopped in build_room, FileExistsError on intro-scene/area-work/tradehouse. The folder held no file: all 167 folders of the try8 area-work tree (58 rooms) were made empty within 0.1 s as the area stage started. Cause: in try8 chim-room-batches (its roots include intro-scene) ran beside the area stage and saw the room folders appear; Recorder.close gave the shared files to the traced writer (the area stage, BUILD-REUSE-ATTRIBUTION-33) but left the folders in the observer record, so the chim-room-batches reuse plan (2,959 folders) made them (apply_stage, plan directories) and the area stage room build, which creates its folder with exist_ok False, stopped. Same class as BUILD-SHARED-WRITES-UNATTRIBUTED-52. Fixed in source: Recorder.close drops from the observer the folders holding none of its own files that the writer filled or made (build_cache.foreign_directories); plan_reuse drops the same from records made before the fix (another stage of the old run filled or made them); build_room takes a room folder that holds only empty folders (prepare_area.room_folder), a file in it still stops the room. Tests: tests/test_build_cache.py WriteAttributionTests (the writer owns the folders it filled; foreign_directories), tests/test_stage_units.py RoomFolderTests. Open: confirmed by dev1-try10. Confirmed (2026-10-26 05:55 +0200 / 2026-10-26 03:55 UTC): dev1-try10 (b5eb61b7, reusing try8) ran the area stage and balmora-interiors through; it stopped later, in chim-town-vivec_city, on SKEL-BUDGET-SHAPES-52.

title: With skeletal actors the game stops loading Balmora at 16 MB of Fast RAM with a software failure (error 80000027); the baked build loads
status: Open (2026-10-26 05:57 +0200 / 2026-10-26 03:57 UTC, SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52): the animation stage image built from 7064ea39 with --npc-anim-type 2 stops at 16 MB of Fast RAM, on FS-UAE JIT and on the slow preset alike. After the console's CHIM zone line for maps/balmora-chim.chim the emulator stops in exec idle, and the screen shows a Software Failure requester for SYS:AmiWind (error #80000027, a TRAP #7: the code the compiler puts at a path it proved invalid, or a deliberate trap). The same stage built with --npc-anim-type 1 loads and plays at 16 MB, and the skeletal build loads and plays at 32 MB and at 128 MB. The game itself names 32 MB as the minimum since v0.0.48 (RAM-REQUIREMENT-32MB-48), but at 16 MB it says it will start, so it must fail gracefully, not trap. Suspects: an allocation of the shared tables (aw_skel_load.c, malloc of the whole table) or of the pose cache failing under the 16 MB heap, with a NULL that a caller does not test. Next: the trap's program counter from the FS-UAE monitor at the alert, mapped with the engine link map. Fixed (2026-10-26 07:02 +0200 / 2026-10-26 05:02 UTC): on a stage build of 484e3455 the table was refused as planned (Animation table: no memory for 654324 bytes, largest free block 252424), and the game then stopped on the same trap in a second malloc: the UAE monitor and the link map put it in MemMap::alloc again, returning into AW_SaveWrite +0x1B6, the 256 KB buffer of the arrival autosave. Fixed in e9fb0407 (gate 3981): aw_tryalloc.h AW_TryMalloc asks exec's largest block first and gives NULL instead of the trap; the three save buffers use it, and a save that cannot get one says Save skipped: not enough free memory for its buffer; previous saves retained. Checked on FS-UAE JIT at 16 MB with stage build 2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev1_miniwind-anim-stage-type2_e9fb0407: Balmora loads and plays, the stage lines up 8 skeletal actors, the beast table is refused (its one Argonian or Khajiit stands in its rest pose), the arrival autosave is skipped with its message, and the run passes (103 s). At 16 MB the skeletal residents fit with the common table only; the remaining malloc sites are SDK-MALLOC-TRAPS-52. Seen in the dev1 image too (2026-10-26 07:29 +0200 / 2026-10-26 05:29 UTC): dev1-try12 (28046c31, before the fix commits) built whole; its 16 MB boot smoke stalled loading Seyda Neen (dbg tp did not load a map, PC in exec idle), so the delivery stopped there. dev1-try13 on b1c72d1b carries 484e3455 and e9fb0407.
where: skeletal residents loading at 16 MB Fast RAM (aw_skel_load.c, model_alias_stream.inc)
severity_reason: 16 MB machines get a software failure instead of the documented slower start

title: The toolchain's malloc never returns NULL: a failed allocation stops the game with Software Failure #80000027 (TRAP #7); 45 engine malloc sites test for a NULL that cannot come
status: Open (2026-10-26 06:15 +0200 / 2026-10-26 04:15 UTC, found by SKEL-16MB-TRAP-52): libc malloc.o of the Amiga SDK (MemMap::alloc, used by malloc, calloc, realloc and the C library's own buffers) makes a request over 32,747 bytes with AllocMem(size + 4), and a smaller one from 32,760-byte pool blocks. When AllocMem returns NULL it stores through it, a path the compiler turned into trap #7, so no allocation failure ever reaches the caller. The engine has 45 malloc calls outside aw_skel_load.c that test for NULL (aw_actors.c, aw_character.c, aw_glut.c voice table, aw_items.c, aw_cam.c, aw_gallery.c, aw_aread.c and others); each one is a Software Failure on a full machine instead of its message. The guard torch probe already uses AllocMem for this reason (aw_guard_torch.c), and the animation tables now check AvailMem first (484e3455). Wanted: one engine allocator for every malloc that can fail (AllocVec with a tracked list freed at exit, or an AvailMem check), and a test that no engine file calls malloc directly. Progress (2026-10-26 07:02 +0200 / 2026-10-26 05:02 UTC): engine/aga/src/aw_tryalloc.h AW_TryMalloc (e9fb0407, gate 3981) is the allocator that can say no. Its rule matches the toolchain allocator's: a request over 32,747 bytes needs a block of size + 4, a smaller one needs a 32,760-byte pool block, and 16 KB is kept spare. The save buffers (aw_save.c) use it, and the animation tables have their own check (aw_skel_load.c, 484e3455). The other malloc sites are still open. Fixed in e1ab51c5 (2026-10-26 07:47 +0200 / 2026-10-26 05:47 UTC, gate 3992): all 45 engine malloc, calloc and realloc calls in 31 files (engine/aga/src and chim/) go through aw_tryalloc. The new aw_tryalloc.c, in the Makefile, holds AW_TryMalloc, AW_TryCalloc (refuses a count x size overflow) and AW_TryRealloc (NULL keeps the old block). Each asks exec's largest free block for what the toolchain allocator will ask (size + 4 over 32,747 bytes, else a 32,760-byte pool block) plus 16 KB, and returns NULL otherwise. The checked versions are used only on the m68k target (AMIGA and __m68k__): a host test that compiles snd_amiga.c with -DAMIGA and stub headers gets the C library's own. Every caller already handled NULL except the playback-argument path in host.c, which now stops with a message. tests/test_engine_allocations.py fails on any malloc, calloc, realloc or strdup call outside comments and strings in any engine .c, .h or .inc; the allow-list is aw_tryalloc.c and the host macros in aw_tryalloc.h. The source-pinned heap policies were re-pinned (tools/alias_stream_heap.py, edge_cache_heap.py, compact_harvest_heap.py). Also: the Skeletal model ... rest pose line is said once per model, not on every load from the cache. The 16 MB FS-UAE check on a stage build of e1ab51c5 follows. Checked (2026-10-26 07:58 +0200 / 2026-10-26 05:58 UTC): stage build 2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev1_miniwind-anim-stage-type2_e1ab51c5, FS-UAE JIT at 16 MB. The scripted session passed (105 s): Balmora loaded, the beast table was refused (no memory for 654324 bytes, largest free block 251736) and said once, the arrival autosave was skipped with its message, and the stage lined up its cast. A second session with the UAE monitor's breakpoint on the TRAP #7 handler (trap_run.sh) loaded Balmora and played without reaching it.
where: the Amiga SDK libc malloc.o (MemMap::alloc) and every engine malloc call
severity_reason: Any allocation that fails on a full machine stops the game with a Software Failure instead of a message
platform: FS-UAE 3.1.66, A1200 68040, 16 MB Fast RAM (the SDK allocator read with objdump)

title: 50 region-frame entrances cannot be used from where a player can stand: the use ray meets the entrance structure or the ground before the door, or there is no standing spot at it
status: Open (2026-10-26 21:58 +0200 / 2026-10-26 19:58 UTC): found by the new wall check of tools/door_engine_check.py on the v0.0.53-dev2 image. 50 of the 830 region-frame exterior entrances cannot be used from any spot a player can stand on in front of them (straight out from the door's face and toward the room's way-out arrival, at the 56-unit use reach and nearer, looking at the middle, upper and lower part): the use ray meets another placement 1 to 33 units before the door (21: the Daedric shrine oval doors of Kaushtarari, Zergonipal, Assurdirapal, Ebernanit, Ashalmimilkala, Bal Ur, Ashalmawia, Maelkashishi, Assarnatamat, Bal Fell; the Rethan and Indarys Manor fort doors; the End of the World renter rooms; the Neglected Shipwreck cabin), no standing spot within 48 units above the threshold (18: Dwemer ruin doors of Arkngthand, Nchuleft, Dagoth Ur Outer Facility, Sorkvild's Tower; Redoran guard tower and outpost trapdoors; Sarys and Odirniran tombs), the ground in front of the door within the ray (9: Velothi tombs and caves such as Andas, Orethi, Senim, Mababi, Sargon, Zenarbael, Endusal, Bthungthumz) or out of reach (2). Seen in game the same evening (FS-UAE, dev2): Kaushtarari and Ebernanit shrines (no prompt; the player stops 63 units from the door), Sadrith Mora Gateway Inn North Wing (no prompt, the ground 13 units above the threshold) and Arkngthand (the use ray meets the doorway arch 8 units before the door; the ground in front lies over the door's lower part). The original LAND at these doors is at the threshold, so the blocking is in the converted collision of the entrance structures and the ground in front of them, not in the original. The full list: door-engine-check.md of the build (private). The count of usable doors with the wall traced (1,052) is in config/door-check-baseline.json and may only go up. 2026-10-26 23:15 +0200 / 2026-10-26 21:15 UTC: fixed in source for 40 of the 50. Cause of the largest class: the converted collision of an entrance (the Daedric shrine oval doorways, the Rethan and Indarys fort doors, the End of the World renter rooms, the Neglected Shipwreck cabin; the doorway of some Velothi tombs and caves) closes the doorway 1 to 11 units in front of the door's use box, and aw_scene.c aimed_door refused the use when any surface lay more than 1 unit before the box. Now the doorway slack DOOR_USE_SLACK (16 units) lets the use ray meet a surface that near before the door; a wall farther out still refuses it (tests/aga_scene_test.c: 8 units passes, 24 refused; fails on e088083d's aw_scene.c). The door engine check reads the engine's value and its standing model was made closer to the game (a player may stand up to 80 units over the threshold on the doorway structure itself, and on a trapdoor). On the v0.0.53-dev2 image with the new rule: 1,092 of 1,102 usable with the wall traced (was 1,052), all 1,102 after walking in. The CHIM world is not re-keyed: the change is in the engine and the check only. The 10 left are DOOR-USE-COLLISION-FILLED-53 (v0.0.54). 2026-10-26 23:37 +0200 / 2026-10-26 21:37 UTC: in game on the dev2 image with gate 4068's engine (the doorway slack): the Gateway Inn North Wing (Sadrith Mora) and Arkngthand now prompt and enter (the use ray meets their doorway 12 and 7 units before the door); Kaushtarari and Ebernanit still do not: the player slides back down the shrine steps to 62 units from the door, out of the 56-unit reach. The door engine check now also requires a walkable floor where the player stands (Quake's 0.7 normal) and tries spots beside the line out from the door; like for like on the dev2 image: 1,036 usable with the wall traced with the old 1-unit rule, 1,067 with the doorway slack (+31). The 35 left, among them every Daedric shrine whose steps slide, are DOOR-USE-COLLISION-FILLED-53 (v0.0.54). Shipped in v0.0.53 (2026-10-26 23:53 +0200 / 2026-10-26 21:53 UTC): the doorway slack is in; all 1,102 entrances usable after walking in and both ways, 1,067 with the wall traced (+31). The 35 left are DOOR-USE-COLLISION-FILLED-53, v0.0.54.

title: Every gate failed its smoke part: the image it boots lived in an old build run that the automatic Docker cleanup retired
status: Fixed (28 October 2026): the automatic cleanup of that day retired the v0.0.41-dev5 run the smoke booted. The gate smoke image is now a SHA-256-verified copy of the v0.0.54 release image in its own folder (gate-smoke/v0.0.54), the gate defaults to it, and the cleanup protects that name.
severity_reason: No commit could pass a gate until the smoke image was replaced.

title: The GitHub workflow pinned actions/cache v4.2.3, which runs on Node 20, a runtime GitHub retires
status: Fixed (28 October 2026): re-pinned to actions/cache v5.1.0 (Node 24), commit caa296126883cff596d87d8935842f9db880ef25, read from the v5.1.0 tag (git ls-remote) and its restore and save action files (using: node24); tests/test_ci_workflow.py keeps the pin.
severity_reason: Once Node 20 is retired on the runners the cached jobs would stop.

title: The release tag push ran the whole CI test suite again on a commit main had already passed
status: Fixed (28 October 2026), a regression class: the tests job is skipped on tag refs (the dry-run that needs it with it); a tag run keeps only the from-nothing bootstrap. The release publisher waits for main's run once, then tags. A separate hand-over script beside the kit, which waited on CI a second time, is retired: the kit ZIP and its README command are the whole hand-over. Kept by tests/test_ci_workflow.py and a release guard check.
severity_reason: A release waited on a second full test run of an already green commit; a regression class of the hand-over.

status: Fixed in v0.0.55-dev1 (28 October 2026): the persisting list of the CHIM tracker links each report page from docs/bugs/ (ID.md), the register keeps bugs/ID.md; the 45 allowlisted broken tracker links are gone from tests/docs_broken_links_allowlist.json.

title: A worker killed for memory broke its stage's pool and failed the whole build
status: Fixed on v0.0.55-oom (28 October 2026), released in v0.0.55-dev1: completed_map sends the units of a lost worker out again in a fresh pool at half the units in flight, at most twice, each time with one [pool] WARNING: RAM exhausted? line naming the memory and the out-of-memory kills; a third loss ends the map. Scheduling only: no stage key changes. tests/test_pool_lost_worker.py kills a real worker.
severity_reason: One worker lost to the out-of-memory killer threw away hours of a build instead of slowing it down.

title: Requested: the Toolkit build monitor shows the build's memory: RAM used and available, a memory curve beside the cores, the peak
status: Fixed on v0.0.55-oom (28 October 2026), released in v0.0.55-dev1: the left panel shows RAM: used, available (orange under 20 percent, red under 10 percent available) and the peak with the stages that ran then; the timeline draws the memory curve beside the cores with its peak; the build log gets a [memory] line at each new peak above 75 percent and a WARNING every 5 minutes under 10 percent available; a build without a container records the machine's memory.
severity_reason: A build starving for memory looked like a slow build; only the cores were shown.

title: A reload of the Toolkit always opened the World tab instead of the tab that was open
status: Fixed on v0.0.55-oom (28 October 2026), released in v0.0.55-dev1: the open tab is kept in the address (#monitor) and a reload opens it again.
severity_reason: Watching a build meant picking the Monitor tab again after every reload.

title: Requested: a build in the monitor's Recent builds and gates list opens that run with one click
status: Fixed on v0.0.55-oom (28 October 2026), released in v0.0.55-dev1: a magnifier on every row whose run folder the monitor can read (and a click on its name) opens that run and highlights the row.
severity_reason: A finished run could be opened only from the run list at the top.

title: Requested: the Toolkit build monitor gathers every warning of a build in one yellow row, Warnings: N with a view of the lines
status: Fixed in v0.0.55-dev2 (28 October 2026): the progress writer reads the new lines of every stage log at each snapshot and keeps the warning lines (WARNING anywhere, the underuse lines, the scheduler's alarms and memory cuts) with their time and stage, up to 200, in build-progress.json; the monitor shows a yellow Warnings: N row under the RAM line, [view] opens the list, hidden at 0. tests/test_pool_lost_worker.py.
severity_reason: Warnings scrolled past in the stage logs; a starving or retrying build looked like a slow one.
